#3629. Most, though not quite all, of the 34 fired Rockstar employees are named in the GTA 6 credits

Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the company making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

But perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union."

#3628. PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:

Rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take."

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

#3627. Zara Tindall Shows Cheltenham Why She's The Queen of Race Day Dressing

Zara Tindall didn’t let the cold snap stop her from enjoying a day at the races on Friday. Accompanied by her close friend Dolly Maude and country-set favorite fashion designer Jade Holland Cooper, the daughter of Princess Anne and granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II brought a dash of regal glamour to the proceedings following a glitzy night out in support of Prince William.

And while the sun may have been out, the Olympic equestrian still needed to wrap up against the chill. Tindall opted for a long plaid coat from L'Agence, a Purdey roll-neck jumper in brown, and a fascinator from Sally-Ann Provan. She accessorized with a new pair of Hector Lion earrings, a new Fairfax & Favor handbag, and completed the look with leather boots, also from Fairfax & Favor.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

Dolly, on the other hand, wore an avant-garde feather coat with knee-high boots and what looked to be a pair of emerald tights.

The pair were last spotted together in October, when they attended the William Hill Showcase Meeting at Cheltenham, but their friendship goes way back. Long considered Zara’s best friend, Dolly became Princess Anne’s lady-in-waiting in 2024. A former NHS midwife, she helped to deliver Zara’s third child, Lucas Tindall, on the floor of Zara’s bathroom at Gatcombe Park after the plan for the birth went awry in 2021.

Jade Holland Cooper and Zara Tindall on day one of The November Meeting at Cheltenham racecourse

But Dolly’s bond with the niece of King Charles III goes back long before that. (Not for nothing did Zara’s husband, Mike Tindall, joke that the 53-year-old is “more important than I am.”) Dolly was Zara’s maid of honor when the pair tied the knot, and when Zara split from her then-fiancé, jockey Richard Johnson, in 2003, the pair moved in together—they still live close by in the Cotswolds.

Having worked as a maternity practitioner in the NHS in Gloucestershire for 13 years, Dolly also did some philanthropic work using her maternity expertise, working in the unit of a hospital in Kambia, Sierra Leone for a month in 2013. At Kambia, she taught staff basic nursing skills. Before qualifying as a nurse, Dolly studied fashion and Cordon Bleu cookery at Eastbourne College of Food and Fashion, graduating in 1989.

Zara Tindall also braved the stormy weather for a day at Cheltenham with Dolly in October

Dolly Maude is known for her love of horses—a passion she shares with Zara and Princess Anne—and is often seen in Ascot’s royal box alongside the Princess Royal. In March 2024, she made her first official appearance as the Princess Royal’s lady-in-waiting, a momentous occasion that marked a new phase of her enduring bond with the royal family.

The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

Concerning Dolly’s appointment, another friend of Mrs. Maude's told The Telegraph, “She’s such a great girl. For the Princess Royal, it’s a perfect fit because of their shared love of dogs and horses. She’s not only extremely close to Zara, she also gets on brilliantly with the Princess. She’s fiercely loyal and discreet. It’s a great match.”

While much of Zara Tindall’s time this season has been spent touring the country’s most prestigious racing meets, she still found time to support her cousin, Prince William, at one of his treasured annual traditions. The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

Zara showcased her characteristically elegant style, donning a sapphire-blue Rebecca Vallance short-sleeved midi number, aptly named the “Crown Jewel” dress, which she paired with Kiki McDonough earrings. It is not the first time that the royal has lent her support to Prince William’s second-longest patronage: she also joined the crowd at the Tusk Awards in 2025, donning Rebecca Vallance again, and tearing up at the Prince of Wales’ speech in honor of those who gave their lives as rangers.

#3626. Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other big productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity."

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

The slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again."

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to New Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

Vice City International Airport is on the west side of Vice-Dale County. It's easy to spot with its two giant landing strips in a wedge shape on the southwest side of the city.

#3623. GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

One of the most uncomfortable scenes in You Can See Everything is when co-director Nathan Fielder and surprise star Amanda Seyfried pay a visit to Elizabeth Holmes’ family’s house in Texas after she has been incarcerated on fraud convictions. Billy Evans, Holmes’ partner, and Seyfried get into a contentious discussion over dinner about Evans’ attitude toward Holmes. Evans, who has started talking about the box office hit more and more both in interviews and in a Reddit AMA, recently spoke about the visit, and it turns out he didn’t see what was coming at all. In fact, he thought he was extending a peace offering to Seyfried after her portrayal of Holmes in The Dropout.

Seyfried had already been working with Fielder for some time, and over the course of the second half of the movie, it’s clear she was getting more and more frustrated with Evans as she learned more about him. In fact, she was so upset by Evans’ behavior in the footage she had watched with Fielder that was filmed before Holmes reported to prison in 2023, that she expressed a desire to break the couple up. Evans recently told his side of the story to The Hollywood Reporter, saying of the dinner:

It made more sense to me after seeing the film, and hearing her say, ‘I want to break them up.’ I didn’t understand her intentions [when she came over]. I thought we were extending an olive branch and saying, ‘Look, we’re not angry with you. We’re happy to engage. We don’t blame you for your portrayal of Liz [in The Dropout]. You’re an actress, you didn’t write the script, you didn’t develop the story, you didn’t do the research or lack thereof.’

Seyfried’s intentions were never to ask for forgiveness for playing Holmes at this point. At this point, Amanda Seyfried isn't just the actress who portrayed Holmes. She is also an advocate for her. That’s even more apparent when she plays her again later in the documentary, in the recreations of Fielder’s meetings with the former CEO in the Texas prison. Seyfried had, at that point, developed sympathy for Holmes, which is weirdly exactly what Evans was hoping the film would do, though probably not at his expense. Not like this.

It’s impossible to rank all the wildest moments in You Can See Everything. The more I’ve thought about it over the weeks since I saw it, the more each scene stands out from the others. One day I think Evans taking the bowl of eggs out of Holmes' hand is the craziest; other times it's when Holmes seemingly doesn’t understand “Who’s on First?” That’s not even getting into the disputed scene that features Evans in the shower. However, the dinner confrontation is when I was squirming the most in my seat.

Seyfried pulls no punches in telling Evans what she thinks, and in turn, Evans doesn’t hold back his contempt, either. It’s a scene I can’t wait to watch again when I’m finally able to see the movie on streaming, presumably with my HBO Max subscription, soon.

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

“The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

Gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”

“Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” said Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”

“Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3620. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

#3618. Here’s What Gets Added To A GTA Game Right Before Launch

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rob NelsonRockstar Games

Some big games go gold months before release, meaning theyâre feature-complete and certified to be printed on discs or cartridges for the relevant consoles theyâre coming out on. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick waited until a week before Grand Theft Auto 6âs launch to confirm with 100 percent certainty that it wouldnât get another delay. So what sorts of stuff does Rockstar Games tinker with in the final stretch of a years-long development process?

According to head of production Rob Nelson, it can be adding a last-minute piece of music or tinkering with the open-world polish. In a recent interview with Kotaku, he explained that the team begins to âcircle the wagonsâ two to three months out from launch to see what final fixes, improvements, and additions are achievable before the gameâs initial release.Â

The changes need to get progressively smaller, or they risk creating other problems that can cause last-minute trouble. âWhen you go and you’re messing around with systemic stuff, it’s quite scary,â he said. âWhereas if you’re fixing a piece of scripted content on a mission, less scary, because as long as you fix it there, it’s fine.â

Nelson mentioned that the partner mechanics between protagonists Jason and Lucia were something the team did several final passes on to get just right. He said the free-roam mechanic with the two of them together was particularly challenging to finesse.Â

âIt’s like if you’re going around as them together, it has to hold up if you go into a shop together and buy something, you buy something for the partner, or you go into a club and you can dance together or you go in and you pull a gun on somebody, you jack a carâlike, it has to work,â he told Kotaku. âYou have to basically be able to play Grand Theft Auto with a partner, an AI partner.â

This could include small stuff like suddenly exiting a store or hopping out of a car. Whichever character the player isnât controlling in that moment has to respond immediately and in a way that feels natural. Spontaneity can feel liberating, but it can also lead to jank, and Rockstar wanted to avoid the potential messiness that can come from too much unpredictability.Â

Nelson gave an example of when players go into gang compounds. If Jason or Lucia go to choke someone during stealth, the other will try to follow suit. The same goes for pulling out guns and shooting. This complexity can lead the characters to make mistakes in real time, which is supposed to flow into the larger narrative.Â

âIn that moment you have to make a choice, not as a player but as a partner: Am I going to leave them?â Nelson said. âOr I’m going to start shooting this cop, is that going to then fuck with my criminal profiles? And you have all of this stuff that you’re juggling.â He believes even the messiness of a pathing error can be additive to that sort of experience.Â

Aside from polishing free-roam interactions and scripted sequences, the team spent the final months tinkering with GTA 6âs economy, relationship metrics, and criminal profiles, the reputations that drive how the world reacts to Jason and Lucia. No doubt some or all of that will continue to get tweaked in a parade of post-launch patches during the gameâs first year and beyond.Â

#3617. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

The NCIS franchise is in full swing on the 2026 TV schedule, and that will only continue into the new year. Currently, the Mothership, NCIS: New York, and NCIS: Origins are airing, and come early 2027, NCIS: Sydney will be joining the lineup. Even though it’s exciting that we’re finally going back down under, some fans can’t help but bring up the other shows from the franchise that were unfortunately canceled.

Just this week, he official NCIS Instagram confirmed Sydney Season 4's premiere for this coming January. After that, plenty of people took to the comments to share their thoughts. And not all of the sentiments were positive. Some fans are currently pointing out the sacrifices that have been made to make room for Sydney. That includes cutting Origins’ third season in half, while both NCIS and newbie New York get full seasons. Others are still hurt over NCIS: Los Angeles and NCIS: Hawai’i 's cancellations, as well as the (still-fresh) cancellation of Tony & Ziva:

As someone who is a fan of every single NCIS show, I’m definitely still hurt over having to say goodbye to these axed shows far too soon. Hawai’i’s cancellation definitely blindsided me and others, including series star Vanessa Lachey. Quite frankly, I’m still wondering exactly why the Eye Network decided to end it.

As for Tony & Ziva, fans were hoping CBS would pick up the series after Paramount+ canceled it, but unfortunately, that was not in the cards. It's great that co-lead Michael Weatherly is back on NCIS, but it’s still just not the same. Even amid the announcement of the New York spinoff, there were plenty of detractors speaking out about the canceled NCIS shows. While I understand that the network TV is a business, I can still empathize with the sentiments.

Meanwhile, Sydney’s return marks a change for the franchise that is upsetting fans. Some viewers have been sharing their displeasure over the fact that both Sydney and Origins are not getting full seasons. Instead, the two shows are getting only 10 episodes for their respective seasons. It’s understandable that CBS would do this, given that there’s already too many shows on the schedule, but a 10-installment run just feels way too short.

I, for one, agree with everyone who is hurt over the cancellations and believe that Sydney should have gotten a full season along with Origins. That being said, I will gladly take what I can get, as a 10-episode order is better than nothing. On that note, I'd imagine that plenty of franchise devotees will continue to tune in for the shows that are still airing. However, I don't expect many of them to stop carrying torches for the canceled shows anytime soon.

At the very least, NCIS: Sydney will finally be returning for Season 4 on Tuesday, January 26 on CBS, streaming the next day with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3615. GTA 6 Finally Explains Why You Can Hear The Police Radio Chatter

If you’ve played any of the mainline Grand Theft Auto games, you’ve likely committed a crime and heard a police radio communication reporting your naughty behavior. It’s been a part of the series since the first game. And yet, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first game in the series to actually explain how your character can hear this police chatter.

Early on in Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason’s hacker friend and stoner buddy Cal does the character a solid. He grabs his phone and installs a custom, homebrew police radio scanner program. From then on, Jason can hear the police reporting on his actions, crimes, and location, as was the case in (nearly) every previous GTA game. Later on, when GTA 6 lets you free-roam around as Lucia, she, too, has the same police scanner app installed on her phone. The game doesn’t show Cal installing it, so I’ll just assume it happened off-camera.

Now, to be clear, I don’t think Rockstar needed to dedicate any time or effort to explaining how players could hear police radio chatter in GTA. Sure, sometimes I’d think about how it was possible for characters like CJ or Tommy Vercetti to hear the police reporting on their crimes, but then I would just remind myself it’s a video game, and games are filled with stuff that doesn’t make sense. Characters die and then respawn. Protagonists never age. And you can hear the police radio chatter despite not having a scanner. Just usual video game-y nonsense.

Still, I think it’s fun that for GTA 6, Rockstar took the time to explain how Jason and Lucia can hear the police radio chatter. And it also factors into gameplay. Our protagonists know if the police have spotted their car or have reported their clothing. They even mention it during chases as they try to make their escape, so it’s important we understand that the characters, and not just the player, can hear the chatter. In past games, you could just assume it was a gameplay mechanic, and the protagonists didn’t hear the radio messages. Not so in GTA 6.

I guess Rockstar felt like it was finally necessary to provide a grounded explanation for this classic GTA feature.Â I await Rockstar explaining why every state in the GTA universe is an island in Grand Theft Auto 7.Â

#3614. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

In unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just announced that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form."

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal

Hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

#3613. Yes, You Can Keep Playing GTA 6 After The Credits Roll And Don’t Worry, That’s Not A Spoiler

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a very, very big game with tons of main missions, side missions, activities, random events, races, and more to find and complete. So you might feel compelled to clear out the map before reaching the finale. But you don’t need to do that.

In past Rockstar Games, like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2, the studio has let players return to the open world after finishing the main story. However, how this has been handled has varied. In RDR2, you take on the role of another character who can complete activities and side missions after the credits roll. In GTA IV, the game just lets you keep playing post-credits as Niko. This is how it works in most GTA games, actually. Things are a bit different in GTA 6.

Instead, before you enter the final mission, which took me about 90 hours or so to reach in my playthrough, the game makes a big point of asking if you want to go forward with the finale or not. Once you wrap up that big, multi-mission finale and see one of the game’s main endings, GTA 6 tosses you back in time to that moment when you were asked if you wanted to finish the story or not. But this time, Jason and Lucia say no; they aren’t ready, and head back out into Vice City. At that point, you can keep playing GTA 6, wrap up everything on the map, and explore. (The finale mission marker remains on the map if you want to finish the game again and possibly get a different ending.)

It’s an interesting way to handle the endgame and is unlike any past Grand Theft Auto. It also lets GTA 6‘s ending go in a lot of different directions, depending on your choices. I’m not going to even hint at what those endings are, but I’ve seen two of them and trust me, they play out in wildly different and sometimes surprising ways.

The one downside to this approach is that GTA 6 feels a bit frozen in time at the end of the game. No new major storylines can be introduced, as they would possibly get in the way of the narrative wrapping up.

But hey, once you beat the final mission, you unlock the ability to reach 100 percent completion and even unlock the ability to complete challenges to reveal in-game cheat codes that let you go wild in Vice City. So consider it a vacation for Jason and Lucia after all your hard work as a criminal.

Jennifer Svedberg-Yen says she left the studio in July after finishing up work on the studio's hit RPG.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive. In an interview with Gamesbeat, Svedberg-Yen said she wants to return to her own creative efforts, including stories for film and television, and also aims to set up a new fund specifically to support the advancement of narrative design in games.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards. That makes it particularly interesting that Clair Obscur is Svedberg-Yen's one and only game credit: Prior to joining Sandfall Interactive in 2020 as one of its earliest members, she spent years working in the finance industry.

Despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year. "I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she said. "We’ve parted ways."

That has to hurt for Sandfall, but Svedberg-Yen still has ambitions within the game industry, including the creation of an investment fund for "narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers."

"This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face," Svedberg-Yen said. "To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.

"In that way I can also help them build a stronger narrative foundation from the beginning. I’ve done a lot of consulting work with different studios. I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."

Svedberg-Yen said a lot of studios think of narrative as "a skin," something thrown on near the end of the development process once everything else is assembled. But that's like trying to solve a puzzle without knowing whether there's actually a solution at all, she continued, "whereas if you start from the very beginning, when everyone is starting from the same jumping-off point, everything will naturally be able to tie together."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The goal is not to compete with publishers, she explained, but "to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make."

That investment fund, alongside her own projects and stories, will be Svedberg-Yen's primary focus in the coming year: "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of Dancing with the Stars.

Last night was the semi-finals of Dancing with the Stars on ABC (and streaming with a Disney+ subscription), and it was a doozy. The power of the fan vote was once again shown, as Harry Shum Jr. was eliminated despite having two perfect scores. His final dance was a tribute to his time on Glee, including some kind words about late actress Naya Rivera. It was a moment hat made me cry, but what was going on in the background at the Skybox made me irate.

The last two weeks saw DWTS contestants with dance experience voted off, largely thanks to the fans. Harry Shum Jr'.s final performance was to the Glee version of "Valerie", with him pointing up to heaven after the final pose, and talking about Naya Rivera to host Juliane Hough in the Skybox. It was a beautiful way to honor the late actress, but it was spoiled a bit by pros Alan Bersten and Brandon Armstrong recording content for the TikTok live in the background.

As you can see in the above photo, Bernsten and Armstrong were in full view as Shum talked about Rivera, clearly emotional and saying how much the Glee cast misses her. It even looked like he had shed a tear during the dance, which makes two of us. So when I saw the two pros in the shot pulling focus, I basically screamed at my TV. I know they probably didn't mean it, but it felt disrespectful to see them shooting content in the midst of this emotional moment.

Even before Harry Shum Jr. spoke about Naya Rivera, the late actress' presence was felt throughout his quickstep. Rather than dancing to the Amy Winehouse version of "Valerie" the Dancing with the Stars band performed the Glee arrangement that was famously sung by Rivera in one of the show's most iconic moments. What's more, a few dance moves were even lifted straight from the choreo performed by Shum and Heather Morris in that number. You can check out that quick moment below.

A post shared by Virtual Reali-Tea by Page Six (@virtualrealitea)

When Harry Shum Jr. pointed up at heaven after his final pose, it was clear that Naya Rivera was on his mind. The tribute became all the more clear up in the Skybox, with the Grey's Anatomy star telling Hough:

I feel like Dancing with the Stars is synonymous with Glee. Just the Glee that comes out of it. To be able to dance with Naya's version, it means so much to so many people including myself. We miss you, babygirl.

This was a classy and touching tribute to Shum's late co-star, which is why the juxtaposition between his words and Alan Bersten and Brandon Armstrong doing a bit for the TikTok live felt so upsetting. The pros were just doing their job, but I wish they were listening and reading the room during this emotional moment.

New episodes of Dancing with the Stars air Tuesdays on ABC as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Harry Shum Jr.'s elimination was a shock, but he went out on a high note with two perfect scores and paying respect to Naya Rivera.

#3610. Wow, GTA 6 Has Some Incredible Animations

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar GamesTiny Details

Grand Theft Auto 6, out now on Xbox and PS5, is a very big game. But don’t assume it’s just a blandly massive world with no tiny details to discover. Rockstar Games has packed GTA 6 with more detail than any of its previous games, including some truly impressive animations.

Let’s start with one of the earliest animations I spotted that truly made me go “Whhhooooaaa…” I parked too close to a car, and Jason was unable to fully open his door. In past GTA games, this would lead to the character teleporting out of the car or the door clipping through the other vehicle. In GTA 6, that’s not the case. Instead, Rockstar has added a dedicated animation for Jason and Lucia where they squeeze in and out of the car.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is filled with tiny animations like this that often made me shake my head and think, “I guess I get why this took so long to make.” For example, there are so many animations connected to eating and drinking in this game. I mean, you can crack open a cold one with one hand while holding and shooting an assault rifle in the other.

I also discovered that Jason and Lucia can eat a burger while holding a soda at the same time and even switch between them whenever. And when your drink is empty, you can toss it in a nearby trash can with a procedural animation that doesn’t always work. I’ve missed the trash before, and I felt like an asshole. Jason and Lucia might be murderers who rob and steal, but they aren’t litterbugs!

One animation that really caught me off-guard happened when I was testing how much damage cars in GTA 6 can take before they stop working. I found an empty parking lot, lined up my car with a nearby wall, and floored the accelerator. I expected to slam into the wall and total the front of my vehicle. Instead…

Again, GTA 6 has so many surprising animations and details. I can’t list them all here because I know I’ve not found them all yet. Maybe I never will? Regardless, I highly recommend you poke around GTA 6 and try stuff out because you’re likely to find some wild detail or tiny animation you’ve never seen before.

And for those who want to see a few more, here’s a video compilation I put together of some tiny animations I spotted while playing GTA 6 over the last few weeks. No spoilers are included in the video below.

#3609. Christine Quinn Talks Divorce, New Love and Her ‘Selling Sunset’ Return

When we sit down to chat with Christine Quinn about her highly anticipated return to Selling Sunset, she’s everything we want her to be and more: whip-smart, gorgeous, funny and ready to spill the tea. She’s also surprisingly — and endearingly — anxious about doing her first big interview in some time. “I’m so sorry,” she tells Us a few questions in. “I’m a little nervous!”

Much has happened during the 38-year-old’s hiatus from the hit Netflix reality series, which follows real estate agents at the Oppenheim Group as they wheel and deal with L.A.’s rich and famous. After leaving the show in 2022 following a five-season run, Quinn split from her husband of four years, entrepreneur Christian Dumontet, in early 2024. Dumontet was arrested in connection with an alleged domestic violence incident involving their son, Christian, and was later arrested again for violating an emergency protective order. That April, he filed for divorce and requested legal custody of Christian. Amid the ordeal, Quinn moved back to her home state of Texas with their son, now 5, to be closer to her parents and sister. Looking back on that period, she tells Us, “I’m so glad I’m safe, and I’m so glad that my son is safe.”

Today, she’s ready for the spotlight again, and superfans couldn’t be more excited. The author of 2022’s How to Be a Boss Bitch is beloved for her no-nonsense attitude, quick wit and over-the-top style, but she insists she’s mellowed out — just a bit. “A lot has changed since viewers last saw me, and I think they’re going to be pleasantly surprised,” Quinn says. “I’ve grown so much. I’m still the same Christine, just a little softer and more vulnerable.”

Ahead of the season 10 premiere (all episodes available December 4 on Netflix), Quinn opens up to Us about where she stands with her Selling Sunset castmates, finding love again and why she insists she’s a lot more down to earth than people realize.

It’s been a while since we’ve seen you on our TV screens. Welcome back! I really never wanted to leave. But mentally, I had to for myself. I had my son, and my marriage was falling apart. It was a lot. Even though it’s [only] been four years, it feels like so long ago. And then when I got back into it, it was like no time had gone by. I’ve always had a special place in my heart for the Oppenheim Group and for real estate. So the timing was right. It felt good. I was thrilled.

What made you decide to return? Obviously a lot happened in my life; I got divorced and had some lessons I needed to learn. [Back when I was filming], I was married to someone who was not supportive, and there was a lot of tension between me and my work and the office. [After] my circumstances changed, I was like, “OK, what do I want? Who am I?” So when I got approached to do the show, I was like, “Absolutely.” I’ve always loved Selling Sunset. It’s my first love, my baby.

Did you have any reservations? Even though it was an obvious yes, it was not easy because I live in Texas, so dropping everything and coming out here for three months was a tough decision. But I knew it was the right one for me and my son. I missed him, but he was here every weekend with me. We wouldn’t go more than four days without being together. But I definitely had reservations. I worked so hard to have peace in my life.

What was it like to film again? I was nervous. I hadn’t met these girls; I didn’t have preexisting relationships with anyone except Heather [Rae El Moussa] and Amanza [Smith]… And there are a lot of big personalities. I was also nervous about getting back in the groove. I was like, “Am I going to be able to balance all of this? Can I handle it?” I don’t know how, but I did!

You’ve talked about being portrayed as the villain. Any concerns about that happening again? It’s hard because people are like, “She’s a villain.” I’m like, “Guys, you know we all have our levels, right?” We’re all villains in our own way. But [show producers] Adam DiVello and Jason [Oppenheim] made me feel comfortable. They were like, “We’re on season 10. It’s not gonna be dark or petty. We want it to be light and fun. Let’s bring that energy back.” That’s what got me because I love to make people laugh. Sure, I love to be a bit of a bitch sometimes, but there’s a balance.

Was anything off-limits for you? I wasn’t sure how much I was going to share about my marriage and my current relationship. But I realized it was best for me to talk about what I’ve been through and what life can be like on the other side. I’m comfortable and confident in who I am now. I really had a problem with vulnerability and talking about relationships and expressing myself. [Now] I just felt like the time was right to be myself and share my story. I think the audience is going to love it.

When you left the show in 2022, you’d fallen out with most castmates. Do you feel responsible for that in any way? It’s always difficult when you’re in an office with all girls. There’s gonna be drama. From day one, I’ve been really honest about my feelings and observations. Not everyone likes it, but I don’t tell a lie. I needed to be myself, and if in the process there was some collateral damage, I hate that that happened.

Looking back, is there anyone you feel you should apologize to? No. I don’t think there’s anything that I would’ve changed other than perhaps my delivery. Sometimes we get heated and we say things that we [don’t mean]. I wish things could’ve come across a little softer.

Does anyone owe you an apology? Everyone! I’m joking, but it is exhausting having the Cassandra complex. It’s just as damaging being too early to a situation. I’ve learned to be like, “Maybe I’ll shut my mouth and let this play out.”

Have you felt vindicated by a specific cast member’s behavior? I was definitely right about Chrishell [Stause]. People’s eyes were opened. I’m like a truffle pig. I can smell a biatch from a mile away.

In June, you said “the trash needed to be taken out” before you returned. Can you elaborate? Some of these girls are just bad leftovers, and if you leave fish out too long, it reeks up your house. It was time. We needed a mix-up. The energy was getting dark and vile, and it wasn’t fun for anyone. That’s what I’ve heard.

Would you have returned if Chrishell were still on the show? [Stause had accused Quinn of planting stories about her allegedly cheating on her ex-husband; Quinn claimed Stause got special treatment on the show and neglected to congratulate her on her pregnancy. Both women deny the other’s accusations.] I never had a problem with Chrishell. I don’t hold grudges. It’s not who I am. The animosity wasn’t from me. I was willing to be in rooms with her. Even though we had disagreements, I could still show up to work. So I wouldn’t have a problem filming with her. Would it be comfortable? Probably not for her. But she’s doing her own thing [now]. She was on for nine seasons. I don’t think she wants to be on the show anymore.

She’s going through her own split from her partner, G Flip. Perhaps you could bond over that common ground. I can bond and relate to anyone who’s going through a breakup. I never met G. I wish [Chrishell] all the best.

You also weren’t on great terms with Heather. Did you know she was coming back when you signed on? I don’t know the timeline, but I knew she was coming back, and I was excited. We need some familiar faces, and regardless of our situation and our relationship, it was a great decision.

Where do you two stand now? Both on our Louboutins, across the street from each other. I’m kidding. I like Heather. We used to be roommates. We have so much history. Of course we argue like sisters and we have our kerfuffles. But at the end of the day, if we didn’t get upset [it would mean] there’s not real love and feelings there.

Why do you think you guys disagree as much as you do? I’ve always been a lone wolf and done my own thing in terms of having opinions and hard conversations. That’s always kind of set me aside, and I do think there are people who feel more comfortable blending in and having a pack. Sometimes people choose comfort over their own identity.

How has she changed since you were last on the show together? She’s exactly the same — in the best way. Heather’s consistent. Maybe she’s a little hotter? She looks hot! But she’s been married a few years now and has a son as well, and we relate to having toddlers.

How are things with Mary Bonnet? The last time I saw Mary was probably right after my divorce. She was really sweet. I’m not sure what the future holds [about Mary coming back to Selling Sunset], but we all have our stuff we’re working on, and who knows? I haven’t talked to her in a while.

And Emma Hernan? [She and Quinn had tension in season 5 after Hernan alleged Quinn offered Hernan’s client $5,000 to work with Quinn instead; Quinn denied the claim.] I didn’t spend much time with Emma, so I never got the chance to know her. The cultural appropriation empanadas is really not how I roll. [Hernan faced backlash over her vegan empanadas line in 2021.] That’s her thing.

Did you guys work things out? We just moved on. When you’re new and you’re on a TV show, you’re like, “Hmm, how can I get creative?” We’ve all been there. The bribery thing [was the biggest lie about me]. I was just like, “No, I didn’t bribe a client.” They prefer me because I’m a more seasoned agent.

How difficult was it to open up about your marriage while filming season 10? It’s no surprise [that was] the hardest topic, and also how long it took me to get back on my feet. I was kicked to the floor with no life raft. I was hesitant [to open up about it], but I’m using it as a way to support women and to be like, “Listen, like, there’s another side. You can get out of this.” That was the most important lesson for me.

Where does the divorce stand now? It’s almost finalized. It took a really long time because he’s out of the country, and he was evading [his] responsibilities.

Do you remember when you knew the marriage wasn’t working? I was in a really dark place after I had my son. I was dealing with work and tension [with] my ex. I did everything I could to try to make it work. I don’t know if things changed [or] the signs were there all along and I didn’t pick up on it. Maybe. It was something that had been coming for a while.

What weren’t viewers seeing about your marriage at the time? Any marriage is hard. I’ve always had a hard time expressing myself, and I never wanted to look like I had a failed marriage. Was I putting on [an act]? Absolutely, sure. I didn’t want to be humiliated. That’s what women do. We just get through things. It’s not good for us. [Quinn tears up.] Sorry, I don’t talk about this stuff, really.

You don’t have to apologize. Do you think it was harder for you to reach out for help because you have such a strong persona? The dichotomy is fascinating. I built an entire brand on how to be a boss bitch — I literally wrote the book on it. I never wanted to admit failure. But the way that I look at it [now], I’m like, “Nothing can break me down.” This can and does happen to so many other women who aren’t strong enough to stand up for themselves.

You previously told Us you received legal papers from Christian while filming House of Villains. That must have been difficult. He served me intentionally when I couldn’t respond. It’s just nasty and unfair. But that’s what divorces are; you’re never divorcing the person you married. The timing was not by accident.

His arrest for domestic violence was in the news. How scary was that experience for you? It was a really, really dark time. I look back on it now… and I think it’s really important for women to know you don’t have to stick it out just to stick it out.

Did you hear from your former costars? Most people reached out, but not everyone. I wasn’t disappointed because I know these girls and nothing shocks me with them. It gets brought up on the show, so you’ll have to [wait and] see [who I’m talking about].

You were going to work on a crypto real estate venture with your ex. What’s happening with that? No clue. I have no update. [Going into business with a romantic partner] is not something I’d do again. It’s risky.

What advice do you have for other women dealing with similar relationship issues? Lean on your close friends and family. That’s why moving back to Texas was so important for me. You have a support group around you, and they’ll do anything for you. You just have to ask. It took a long time for me to admit that I was seeing some red flags and I needed help. There is a light on the other side, and there’s an amazing man waiting for you — I know because I have one.

Tell Us about this lucky guy! [Quinn’s been linked to business exec Thomas McGarrity since early 2025.] He’s great. He’s amazing. He’s everything my first husband wasn’t. [And he has] hair and abs.

Is he on the show? I didn’t know if I wanted to have my relationship on a show again. I’ve been burned by that formula. But I was comfortable, and everything felt right, and you can have a little sneak peek on the show.

What feels different about this relationship? The most important thing is having someone who’s supportive of you and your career. I didn’t have that, and now I do and it feels so good and like anything’s possible. Like, “Oh, wow, I can do this, and I don’t have to tiptoe around it. I don’t have to be scared.” That’s the best part.

Would you get married again? I’m like Elizabeth Taylor. I’ve always wanted to be married, like, 15 times. I’m not out of [my first one] fully yet, but I absolutely could [see myself getting married again]. If you asked me a year ago, I would have said, “No, definitely not.” But yes. I love hope. I’m a Libra. I love love.

What about more kids? Again, never say never. I’ve thought about it. But it depends on the day.

How’s Texas life? I’m a lot more down to earth than people realize. I’m a homebody. I take my son to school every day. I don’t have a nanny. It’s just me. It’s where I’m from and my sister and parents are there, so it feels great. I go back and forth between L.A. and Texas for work. I get the best of both worlds.

What’s your son like? I think at age 5 they really come online. [Christian] is booted up now; he’s conscious and remembers things and gets excited. Halloween was such a fun time, running around and getting candy… He started [Quinn tears up] — I’m sorry, he started kindergarten recently but before that I was able to fly him out here. He was playing Legos in the Oppenheim Group. I was with him constantly, and if I wasn’t, it was for two, three days [apart].

Will viewers see your son this season? I wasn’t able to have him on the show, and that was difficult because he’s the love of my life and I wanted people to see my relationship with him. Maybe soon. We’ll see.

What’s it like being a boy mom? He loves trains and cars and trucks and building things. He’s an engineer. He’s brilliant and so fun. The clothes are easier with a boy! If I had a girl, the outfits would need to be perfect, but I just throw shorts and a shirt on him, and he’s ready to go. He’s very low maintenance. But he’s still my version of casual, right? [Laughs.]

And what are you wearing to school drop-off? Oh, I look deranged. Definitely sweatpants in the morning. I [also] love jeans. I love a tank top. Scrunchie in my hair. That’s my go-to.

How is coparenting with your ex? There’s no coparenting. I’m the only parent. [I have] full custody. I’m a single mom, and it’s literally just me. There’s no financial help or relationship. In a weird way, I’m grateful.

Why? I’ve seen people coparent, and it’s difficult. It’s really hard with the back-and-forth.

What’s been the hardest part of parenting on your own? The questions around “What is a dad?” and “What is a father?” He hears these words, and he hears me call my dad “Dad.” He was asking questions and I didn’t know how to answer them. You’ll see me navigate it in the show.

How did you approach your wardrobe for your return? It was hard because I have tons of clothes and purses and shoes, but I live in Texas, so when it came time to film, I was like, “Oh, I don’t have earrings and shoes and purses and things to pull together.” My stylist and I had to work overtime. It’s an integral part of who I am on the show. Sometimes we’ll all be like, “We’re gonna go to a coffee shop,” and then it’s like, “Just kidding, we’re gonna have a night out.” I’m like, “I don’t have any clothes for that!”

Looking back at your previous seasons, are there any looks you regret? Honestly, no, because even the flops were still kind of fire. [But] me and Jason were at an open house, and I was wearing, like, a white cab driver hat. I was like, “Oh yeah, this is the best idea ever.” It looked like I had a taxi service. I see clips on TikTok now and I’m like, “Oh God, that was really a choice.”

Have you been happy diving back into the L.A. real estate scene? Being back here and seeing these beautiful views and amazing houses, I’m like, “Oh, my God, this is what I fell in love with.” I have clients in Texas, but L.A. is a different market.

What’s the craziest thing you’ve seen during a showing? I had a beautiful listing in Orange County, an $18 million all-white mansion. The woman came, and I’m showing her the garage and all of a sudden, there’s a person in the car. She’s like, “Oh, my God, there’s someone in the car!” And I’m like, “Did my client murder someone?” She was so freaked out she left. When I went back, I was like, “Oh, wait, it’s a mannequin so he can drive through the HOV lane.” I had to go back and say, “That’s not a real person. It’s a mannequin.”

#3608. Sam Altman Is “Still Unknowable” to Andrew Garfield, Even After Playing the OpenAI Co-Founder in Artificial

In Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this new generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield said about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's important to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”

Barbaro said the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the company, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

For Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more."

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci said. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the issue that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with new distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he said about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”

“They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a big thing.”

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3607. How Long Is GTA 6? Depends On How You Play

As I prepare to pick up and play Grand Theft Auto VI tonight, I’m bracing myself to be in Leonida pretty much non-stop for days, weeks, maybe even months. It just intuitivelyÂ feels like it’s going to be a doozy of a long game, huh?

After all its predecessor, GTA V, takes 32 hoursÂ just to rush through the main story (according to HowLongToBeat), and over 50 if you factor in side content. I’d expect its successor, especially with all the bells and whistles Rockstar is showing off, to take even longer.

With reviews out today, we now have a rough idea of what to expect, and yeah: this game’s gonna take time.

Our own reviewer, Zack, says he saw the credits roll at about 90 hours of gameplay. Granted, he was doing a lot of side content and wandering around and testing stuff, and not everyone will want to be anywhere near as thorough as he was. Zack suggests a speedier player might make it through in around 60 hours. Jeff Gerstmann, in his review, says he beat the game after about 45 hours, maybe 50 if you count some saves he had to reload throughout. Zack doesn’t think you can reasonably finish the story in much less than that.

For those looking for more to do, though, Zack has spent 150 hours in GTA VI and still hasn’t seen everything there is to see or done everything there is to do. Like past Rockstar games, GTA VI will let you keep playing after the credits roll (though in a slightly unusual way), so you’re free to turn Leonida inside out for days on end if that’s what you want to do.

Sorry to all the other games in my backlog, we might be here a while.
