#3587. This Fighting Game Is Nominated For A TGA Despite Development Shutting Down

Earlier today, Geoff Keighley announced all of the nominees for The Game Awards 2026, the annual celebration of gaming held in Los Angeles. Among expected nominees Grand Theft Auto VI, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Control Resonant was one surprising name: 2XKO has been nominated for Best Fighting Game, despite Riot Games announcing the end of the game's lifecycle earlier this year.

Riot announced that "active development" for the fighting game, featuring characters from League of Legends, would end in December 2026. "Over the last few months, we’ve been monitoring 2XKO’s trajectory closely, and what we’ve seen is painting a clear, consistent picture," Riot said at the time. "While a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there’s an incredible community that plays every day, we haven’t seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability,”

Riot's fighter is joined in the Best Fighting Game category by Invincible Vs., Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Avatar Legends, and My Hero Academia: All's Justice. 2XKO is also not the only game on this list whose future is in jeopardy; soon after it launched in April, Invincible Vs. developer Quarter up laid off reportedly 75% of its staff, while saying that future updates were dependent on the game's overall sales.

UPDATE 11/18/2026: Skybound has commented on upcoming plans for Invincible Vs. with the following statement:

"We understand there have been some questions surrounding the future of Invincible VS, but we want to reassure players that we're continuing to support the game and have more content planned. Most recently, we launched Season 2 introducing Angstrom Levy as the game's third DLC fighter, expanding the roster to 21 playable characters, alongside the all-new Challenges Mode, giving players new ways to test their skills and earn rewards. Season 3 arrives in December, bringing additional content, challenges and the newest playable fighter, Agent Spider.

Looking ahead, we have more content planned for 2027, with additional details to be shared soon. We're excited about what's ahead for Invincible VS and look forward to continuing to support the game and its community."

Grand Theft Auto VI received the most nominations for a single game at this year's ceremony with eight, including Game of the Year. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem tied for the second-most nominations with six each, while Phantom Blade Zero rounded out the top three with five nominations. Nintendo earned the most nominations for a single publisher, meanwhile, with 12 across the event's 30 awards.

The Game Awards is set to take place December 10 live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California.

#3586. Derek Hough Addresses Criticism Over His 'Dancing With the Stars' Judging

Derek Hough is weighing in on criticism surrounding his Dancing With the Stars judging as season 35 comes to an end.

“This season, there’s a lot going on. There’s the whole thing about me [giving out] the nines,” Hough, 41, exclusively told Us after the semifinals on Tuesday, November 17, referring to how he gave every routine the same score one week prior.

Despite the conversations online, Hough has remained unbothered.

“The reason why that doesn’t bother me at all is because I think anybody that knows me, if you’ve been to one of my shows, if you see me do what I do, if you see me host, if you see anything you see me do, it’s one thing I’ve always been,” he noted. “I consistently show up.”

The judge defended his choice to “come with 110 percent energy” at all times.

“You come to any of my shows, anybody can attest to that,” Hough added. “So I know that I give my absolute all no matter what. Do I sometimes have an off night? Sure, absolutely.”

Hough has been willing to accept feedback, adding, “I’m not exempt from imperfection. But one thing I do know about myself is, I show up. I show up no matter what and I’m a professional in what I do.”

After spending years as a DWTS pro — and winning six mirrorball trophies — Hough moved behind the judges table, offering his perspective on how the show has changed. “But I do feel like the energy around the show is a reflection of the popularity of the show, right? People are having conversations and things like that,” he said. “I would hope that moving forward, we can move toward more enjoyment and what people like about it versus what you don’t.”

He concluded: “Because I feel like what’s bad is always available. So is what’s good. And where our focus goes, our energy flows. So we want to put more energy and focus into what’s good, into each other, and into the show and into the world. There’s enough bad stuff out there. We don’t need to add more to it.”

In addition to judging on DWTS, Hough is also looking forward to the debut of his and wife Hayley Erbert‘s documentary, The Symphony of Dance, which follows the aftermath of her cranial hematoma. (She underwent emergency surgery in 2023 after a life-threatening brain bleed.)

“For us, it’s a beautiful piece of archival footage to have that just tells her story, tells her story really of resilience and overcoming something that was terrifying,” Hough noted. “But also it is a beautiful journey of returning to the stage, reclaiming a part of herself. That was incredible.”

Erbert, 32, admitted she was initially hesitant about the project. “I always say that I’m a private person living a public life, and so it’s a little interesting sharing something that’s so raw and so horrible,” she told Us. “But honestly, it was receiving messages after the fact when I’ve inspired somebody in some way, whether it was mentally, physically, emotionally. And after that, I was like, ‘You know what? If this can help one more person, then absolutely, I’m all for it.’”

Dancing With the Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET.

#3584. As MAGA Melts Down, MAHA Is Also Breaking Apart—Starting With the Moms

In August 2024, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suspended his presidential campaign and endorsed Donald Trump, bringing his ragtag bunch of supporters—crunchy mamas, anti-vaxxers, and conspiracy theorists; testosterone bros, peptide enthusiasts, and people who put a “COEXIST” bumper sticker on their car in the 1990s—along for the ride. But now that the blue wave or tsunami—pick your tortured water metaphor—has come to pass, the fractures within MAHA threaten to break the movement apart, driven by bitter disappointment with the Trump administration.

“I think we are seeing a fracturing of the MAHA movement as those concerns start pulling people in different directions,” says Sandro Galea, dean of the Bursky School of Public Health at Washington University in St. Louis. Groups that are interested in healthier food are not necessarily the same as groups opposed to vaccines, he points out; it’s not a sure thing that those groups will continue to find common cause.

The crack-up didn’t start with the midterms, though the fact that most MAHA-backed candidates lost certainly accelerated it. Earlier this year, Trump had to withdraw his nomination of MAHA darling Casey Means for surgeon general after her stance on vaccines made it impossible for Republicans to get enough votes to support her confirmation. In May, MAHA ally Marty Makary, the commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, resigned, reportedly because of pressure from the administration to authorize fruit-flavored vapes. And in October, Calley Means—Casey’s brother—resigned from his high-level post under Secretary Kennedy at Health and Human Services, with MAHA outrage on unmet promises growing.

Three days after the midterms, Joe Rogan released a bomb-throwing, names-naming, two-plus-hour interview with Calley Means, in which the former Kennedy adviser used the word “demonic,” possibly in the literal sense, eight times.

The big takeaway was that Susie Wiles seemed to have told Kennedy to go sit in a corner and play by himself. All roads to Trump went through her office, and according to Means, she slow-walked, watered down, or outright quashed many MAHA priorities. According to Means, she did this primarily because of her and her family’s financial ties to lobbying on behalf of big business.

Wiles did not respond to a request for comment, but a spokesperson for Wiles previously told Axios that these allegations were “outrageous, defamatory, and provably false.”

Means argued that MAHA managed some wins: Trump signed an executive order to boost research on the use of psychedelics for treating mental health conditions. The new food pyramid instructs Americans to eat more steak than oatmeal. (In this economy?) There have been other MAHA victories too: The administration made it easier for Americans to get a handful of unproven injectable peptides, including the “Wolverine stack.” Trump signed an executive order in support of regenerative farming. The administration requested changes to the labels on testosterone products in an effort to make the hormone easier to prescribe—good news for Pete Hegseth’s promise of a “high-T Department of War.” It asked food manufacturers to voluntarily phase out some food dyes. It has sought to reduce the number of recommended childhood vaccines.

Means did not cite the United States recently losing its measles-elimination status as a win, though that was also a result of MAHA talking points.

The MAGA-MAHA mind meld provided plenty for the wellness bros, but precious little of what MAHA moms were expecting from their alliance with Trump. Tiffany Cianci, a high-profile MAHA advocate who goes by @thevinomom on Instagram, says the results were “small things,” not the massive systemic changes that had been promised.

In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for HHS pushed back on this narrative, writing, in part, “HHS has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history…Across the federal government, the administration has transformed food and nutrition policy, invested more than $1 billion in regenerative agriculture and farm modernization, and taken action to address harmful chemical exposures.”

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. delivers remarks during an event at HHS in August. The event highlighted a series of 'landmark actions' to improve the nation's food.

For the MAHA moms, there are two original sins of Trump 2.0. The first is the administration’s outright support for glyphosate, an herbicide that has been classified as a probable carcinogen by a World Health Organization agency. The second is its failure to put out a definition of ultra-processed foods, which the movement sees as the first step toward curbing those foods, particularly in school lunches. One was never released; Means alleged to Rogan that ultra-processed-food initiatives such as this were stymied by White House officials including Wiles, who he said told him, “I need sugar money.” Reporting found that food CEOs leaned on the White House to make the definition go away.

A White House official said on background that the definition for ultra-processed food remains a priority and is actively being worked on by relevant agencies. White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said that “the MAHA coalition has found a champion in President Trump…The administration has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming.”

However, the Trump administration has arguably hindered research on ultra-processed foods in other ways. A leading scientist who was studying ultra-processed food’s link to diabetes and obesity took early retirement from the National Institutes of Health last year after NIH officials, he said, censored the reporting of some of his study results because the study didn’t prove the hypothesis of ultra-processed-food addiction as they had hoped it would. If he’s to be believed, one of our best hopes for understanding the health risks of ultra-processed foods exited due to the actions of MAHA officials. (Vanity Fair has reached out to HHS for comment on the allegations of censorship; an HHS spokesperson previously told The New York Times, “NIH scientists have, and will, continue to conduct interviews regarding their research through written responses or other means. We remain committed to promoting gold-standard research and advancing public health priorities.”)

“We do have a food supply that’s nearly 70% ultra-processed food,” says Jessica Knurick, a registered dietitian and science communicator on social media. She counters that many of MAHA’s alleged priorities are aligned with the hopes of public health workers and nutritionists—yet the movement writ large has eroded trust in the very professionals who do that work. “They really want fewer environmental toxins. If you want that, you need strong regulation on corporations,” she says. “They voted in an administration that is decisively deregulatory.”

“All of the things that the MAHA movement claimed to have wanted,” she adds, “this administration has legislated in the exact opposite direction.”

See, for instance, the glyphosate debacle. Instead of curbing the herbicide, something for which he’d long been an advocate, Kennedy got on board with Trump’s support of it, including an executive order that actually prioritized production of the chemical under the bizarre guise of national security. Then the administration supported Roundup weed killer manufacturer Monsanto, now owned by Bayer, in a case before the Supreme Court, which resulted in a decision shielding the company from state-level lawsuits brought by those who believed they’d been harmed by the glyphosate-containing product. (Glyphosate-based Roundup products are no longer produced for the US residential market.)

This flew in the face of everything MAHA believed about Kennedy’s priorities. Vani Hari, a MAHA influencer who goes by the Food Babe, has been called both the Jenny McCarthy of food and a Democratic infiltrator. She thinks that the last nearly two years resulted in some positive change. She also tells me that she’s become somewhat disillusioned: “There have also been deeply disappointing decisions, particularly when it comes to glyphosate and pesticides.”

Despite it all, the HHS secretary continues to be deified by the vast majority of MAHA leaders, who don’t blame Kennedy for these setbacks. Cianci, however, blames just about everyone involved. “What I see within MAHA right now is a fracturing into one very, very small sliver that loves the proximity to power and the fundraising. They unfortunately tied their hitch to the wrong horse, which is partisanship,” she says. “And you have the rest of us that actually want our kids to be healthy.”

Supporters of the Make America Healthy Again movement are seen at a news conference on removing synthetic dyes from America's food supply, at the Health and Human Services Headquarters in Washington, DC, 2025.

If there is a road forward for MAHA, it might be best exemplified by Elizabeth Frost, a community health advocate and the leader of MAHA Ohio. She comes by her skepticism of the pharmaceutical industry honestly, after growing up in Appalachian Ohio during the height of the opioid epidemic. She now runs a political consultancy in the state, which she says works with both parties.

Beginning last year, Frost partnered with epidemiologists from Yale to find out how the people of East Palestine, Ohio, were still being affected by toxic exposures after the 2023 derailment of a train filled with hazardous materials. Frost went to bat for the scientists, lending her local grassroots credibility to their study on water quality in the town.

“I think there is a broader anti-corporate movement in America that hasn’t really been given a home with either established party because both parties have their own pet corporate interests,” she tells me. After Kennedy’s ascent, she had hoped for a focus on the MAHA issues that enjoy broad support. “Vaccines are not the most popular issue even for MAHA. Most people in MAHA would prefer for the majority of time to be spent talking about issues that are a little bit more unifying”—rather than something like Steak ’n Shake’s now using beef tallow for its french fries. “It’s just not where people’s hearts are.”

Speaking of no heart: Stephen Miller has been promoted to chief of staff after Wiles was forced out in the wake of the midterms. Both Calley Means and Secretary Kennedy have celebrated the move. “Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” Kennedy wrote on X.

But some MAHA moms are not so sure about the kraken. Cianci says that within MAHA, “people are very, very, very uncomfortable” with Miller. “If you’re just going to do what you’ve been told to do and take it to the extreme—he’s like the human embodiment of the paper clip problem,” she says.

Frost is similarly concerned about how things might go under Miller. “I don’t expect that on environmental exposures, industrial contamination, a strong streak against corporate influence—I doubt we’re going to get those things,” she says. She is also dismayed by MAHA leadership’s embrace of convicted rapist Russell Brand. “What the hell are we doing?” she wonders.

A person familiar with MAHA thinking who spoke on background counters that while it’s fair to say that Miller might be polarizing, he is also not beholden to corporate interests the way Wiles was, making him far less likely to block the scrutiny of pesticides and healthy food policies.

Cianci, Frost, and Hari all hope that MAHA will survive by focusing on policy over partisanship. “I also believe MAHA’s future must be bipartisan,” Hari wrote in an email.

Cianci sees opposition to data centers as the next big issue on which MAHA can lead. And she hopes that the anti-corporate tilt she sees in MAHA will spread. “We had a record number of candidates get elected to Congress this year that turned down all corporate PAC money. That is indicative of the MAHA movement. That is indicative of anti-corruption. And I think they’re going hand in glove.”

Frost would like to see Republicans work with progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on shared goals, like getting pesticides out of the food supply. She wants legislators to realize that “the way to hold their seat is to work across aisles on issues that their constituents care about.”

Perhaps MAHA can reinvent itself by leveraging some of its most popular issues to make common cause with Democrats. After all, 30% of midterm voters told pollsters that they support the MAHA movement, while many more—the vast majority of Americans—say that food additives and pesticide use should be more regulated. A plurality of Americans do not want data centers in their communities. The movement’s best hope for staying relevant is probably the (currently very pissed) MAHA moms, whose concerns about food and pollution were always the most broadly resonant parts of the MAHA platform—rather than a yen for peptides, beef tallow, or testosterone.

Most people want to be able to afford healthy food and effective health care. Trump’s rule has not made those things more accessible, with high cost of living, massive cuts to Medicaid, the ending of certain Affordable Care Act subsidies, and reductions in federal funding for SNAP benefits.

The challenge with a rebrand is that the connection to MAGA is right there in the name. But Trump’s presidency clearly has a shelf life, and MAHA wants to outlast him. “If anyone has any ideas on how to change the name of a political movement,” Frost says, “let me know.”

#3583. BioWare Is Dead, But Mass Effect’s Spiritual Successor Exodus Just Gave Us A Glimpse of A Spicy Romance

For the first time since its announcement during December 2023's The Game Awards, players are getting a look at the female player-character from its upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus--which was full of Mass Effect DNA back when we previewed it in September.

The default female version of main character Jun Aslan was revealed today via a seven-minute featurette showing off both female-Jun's face and a bit more of the game itself. The trailer also provided a glimpse of a brief romance scene between female-Jun and Suliman, who is one of the game's romanceable NPCs.

When GameSpot previewed the game, only male-Jun was playable, and we didn't get a chance to romance Suliman, but we did manage to earn his approval, suggesting he may be into both masculine and feminine Jun. We also didn't see the character creator, but there certainly appears to be one, as we see Jun sporting a different look during the romantic encounter with Suliman, with voice actress Carina Corti (Mafia: The Old Country, Little Death) providing Jun's voice throughout both scenes.

Jun's male character model recently got a complete makeover after players complained his original look wasn't pleasing to the eye, but up until today, it wasn't clear who was voicing him. Today, Archetype shared that Stephen Oyoung (Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Spider-Man 2) will be voicing the character.

The female-Jun reveal is followed by a featurette called Scrappy Salvager, featuring a behind-the-scenes look at Jun's origins and the way players' decision can impact Jun's trajectory early on in the game.

"We think of players as the co-authors of our story, and that applies to Jun as well," game director Chris King explains in the video. 

Art director Mark Anderson describes Jun as a "little fish in a really big pond," rather than starting off as a typical hero ready to save the world. Additionally, the featurette goes into more detail about Jun's "precognition" ability, which allows them to see glimpses of possible futures. If interpreted correctly, these premonitions may help players make choices that benefit them. But misunderstanding them may lead to consequences that expand far beyond Jun and their friends. Due to the way the game's time dilation mechanic works, player choices can have unexpected effects that impact civilizations for centuries.

After the death of BioWare, it seems the Mass Effect formula will live on in Exodus, with its vast worlds, strange alien races, NPC romances, and narrative choices. It shouldn't come as a surprise, of course--Exodus developer Archetype Entertainment was founded in 2019 by BioWare veterans James Ohlen, Drew Karpshyn, and Chad Robertson.

Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

#3582. School Administrator Charged With Sex Crimes Involving Children Is Fired

Authorities are looking for possible victims of a New York school administrator and longtime youth leader who’s charged with sex crimes involving children.

John Henry Griffiths, of Yorktown, who most recently worked as interim assistant principal at Grady Elementary and Dixson Primary Schools in Elmsford, was arrested Monday, November 16, according to the Westchester County District Attorney’s Office.

He’s charged with promoting a sexual performance by a child younger than 17 and possessing a sexual performance by a child less than 16, the district attorney’s office said in a news release.

“John Henry Griffiths has spent [the] last 30 years working in education and volunteering with local youth organizations, affording him access to children throughout Westchester County,” Westchester County District Attorney Susan Cacace said in a Tuesday, November 17, statement. “We encourage anyone who may have been victimized or who may have information about other potential victims to contact my office.”

Since 1996, Griffiths has worked at schools throughout Westchester County, including Croton-on-Hudson, Somers, Pelham and Garrison in addition to Elmsford.

He previously served as the principal at the Garrison School, attended by students in kindergarten through eighth grade, and as the assistant superintendent of the Croton-Harmon Union Free School District, per The Journal News.

Following a tip from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, state troopers executed a search warrant at Griffiths’ home and seized his digital devices, according to New York State Police.

On Friday, November 13, Griffiths, 62, was found to have child sexual abuse material of a girl estimated to be between 6 to 8 years old, the district attorney’s office said. He also allegedly was found to have shared child sexual abuse material of a boy around 11 to 13 years old.

That day, Griffiths was fired from his position as interim assistant principal at Grady Elementary and Dixson Primary schools in Elmsford, according to the office.

Griffiths is involved in Boy Scouts of America, which has been rebranded to Scouting America, the district attorney’s office said. He’s been the scoutmaster of a local troop in Yorktown Heights since 2013.

Griffiths also serves as the minister of music at St. Mary’s Church in Mount Vernon, according to the church’s website. He’s held the position since 2008, according to authorities.

Scouting America and the church didn’t immediately return requests for comment from Us.

Elmsford Union Free School District Superintendent Susan Yom said in a statement that the district learned of the investigation into Griffiths on Friday and fired him, according to News 12 Hudson Valley.

“The District takes its responsibility to protect students and staff extremely seriously,” Yom said. “Our commitment to the safety and well-being of our school community is unwavering, and we will continue to take appropriate measures to protect our students, families, and staff.”

Following an arraignment, Griffiths was detained at the Westchester County Jail, according to the district attorney’s office.

It’s not immediately clear whether he retained legal counsel or entered a plea.

Griffiths is scheduled to return to court on November 24.

If you or someone you know is experiencing child abuse, call or text Child Help Hotline at 1-800-422-4453.

The world's most famous spy comes with a pretty distinguished welcome committee.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I've spent the last couple of days watching people react to Robert Pattinson's James Bond casting, and the responses have been all over the place. Fans have opinions, naturally, and Jon Stewart even found a way to complain that Pattinson already has Batman. However, the reaction I really didn't see coming was from the British Royal Family. Apparently, somebody running the official account knows their 007 history. In addition to that, Ian Fleming's estate also weighed in.

The casting news broke Monday, at which point Amazon MGM Studios used a brief clip to confirm Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the next Bond. Shortly afterward, the Royal Family's official Instagram account popped into the comments on the announcement post with a welcome that was short, clever and perfectly suited to King Charles' reign:

Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr Bond.

Okay, that's pretty good. It's a play on On Her Majesty's Secret Service, the 1969 Bond movie starring George Lazenby, and a nod to the change in monarch since Bond's last big-screen adventure. I'm not saying the palace's social media team needs to write Bond 26, but I wouldn't mind seeing what they'd do with a martini joke.

As much as I enjoyed the Royal surprise, I was even happier to see the Ian Fleming Estate weigh in. The organization, along with Ian Fleming Publications, posted a much longer welcome on X, reaching back to the original Bond novels for something a little more thoughtful than the usual casting congratulations. The statement began:

The Ian Fleming Estate and Ian Fleming Publications are delighted to welcome Robert Pattinson to the James Bond family. As Bond himself reflects at the end of Moonraker when facing the fact that the object of his affections is engaged to another man, 'He must play the role which she expected of him. The tough man of the world. The Secret Agent. The man who was only a silhouette.'

I love that they chose that particular passage from Moonraker. Think about how many actors have stepped into Bond's shoes since Sean Connery first wore the tuxedo. Everybody recognizes the silhouette, but the person inside it has changed quite a bit over six decades. The statement continued:

We look forward to Pattinson stepping into that silhouette and making it his own. We have no doubt that Ian Fleming would be amazed at the longevity of his creation and the fact that the world is still hungry for tales of the world’s greatest spy. As the custodians of Ian Fleming's literary work, we wish Pattinson and everyone associated with the film the very best of luck. And as die-hard fans, we can’t wait for Bond 26.

That's a lovely endorsement, especially since casting a new Bond tends to spark strong opinions. Fan reactions to Pattinson's casting have been pretty mixed, and I'm sure there will be plenty more debate once a trailer for his first 007 flick arrives. I appreciate that Fleming's estate welcomed him by reminding everyone why the character has survived so many reinventions.

Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve will direct Pattinson's first outing, with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writing the script. The next Bond film doesn't have a confirmed release date yet, so don't expect it to be part of the 2027 movie release schedule. That's because there's still a long way to go before we see what kind of 007 he'll be.

For now, Robert Pattinson has received congratulations from the people looking after Bond's books and a cheeky greeting from the Royal Family. That's a pretty memorable way to start a new job.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3577. WoW: Forever Exploit Lands Streamers In Hot Water After Farming Thousands Of Gold

A lucrative World of Warcraft: Forever dungeon-farming exploit that netted some players hundreds of gold per hour has been hotfixed, and Blizzard is taking action against accounts that (temporarily) walked away with thousands in loot.

For the dedicated few who have already reached max level in the new version of Blizzard's MMORPG, a new endgame dungeon, Blackmaw Hold, proved to be quite lucrative. In the dungeon, a room with 30 non-elite enemies proved to be the perfect spot for area-of-effect gold farming, since it's easy to access.

As detailed by Wowhead, the farm was as simple as running to the room in question, killing all the mobs, looting them, resetting the dungeon, and repeating. Not only did the enemies drop anywhere from 25 to 50 silver each, but they also dropped items that could be sold either to a vendor or on the auction house for even more profit.

And some players, including prominent streamers, did just that during Forever's second weekend. One streamer, Ziqo, who was previously in hot water for accepting illegal gold during the game's beta, revealed he made 4,000 gold from the farm. On stream, Ziqo named other streamers who did the same and said his only regret was choosing to sleep for four hours instead of farming longer.

On places like the WoW: Forever subreddit, players worried about the effect such a huge amount of questionably obtained gold would have on the MMO's economy, especially since the game has been out for less than two weeks. Many called on Blizzard to take action against accounts, including streamers, who benefited from the farm.

Blizzard issued a hotfix on November 16, making the enemies from Blackmaw Hold no longer drop loot. In a forum post the following day, Blizzard explained what went wrong and why it was taking action. While Blizzard said finding good farming spots is part of old-school WoW, the enemies players were farming in Blackmaw Hold were incorrectly dropping loot that would normally be reserved for elites, an obvious mistake.

Players who ran the dungeon a few times and "benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong" and don't need to worry, Blizzard said. However, a few "hundred players worldwide" spent "significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies."

Those players are now in more serious trouble. Blizzard locked their ability to engage in Forever's wider economy following the exploit, and said it is removing gold they earned through "exploitative gains." Additionally, "significant abusers" of the exploit will be handed account suspensions.

"As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended," Blizzard said. "We will continue to take action against intentional abuse."

The Blackmaw Hold farm wasn't the first gold controversy in Forever, and it certainly won't be the last. During the game's beta, streamers were caught accepting suspicious amounts of gold and encouraging their communities to illegally buy gold on their behalf. As a result, Blizzard issued suspensions, made in-game changes, and made it clear it would crack down not only on accounts selling illegal gold, but also on those buying or accepting it.

Farming exploits aside, Forever's launch has been relatively smooth, though Blizzard can't seem to decide how much experience players should get in dungeons. Despite Forever's launch breaking WoW concurrent-player records, it still wasn't enough to get the MMO nominated for Best Ongoing Game at The Game Awards 2026.

#3576. Stephen Baldwin Opens Up About ‘Life-Changing’ Heart Disease Scare

Stephen Baldwin gained a new perspective on life after he experienced a frightening medical emergency over the summer.

“I was at home, and I got this kind of fluttering on my chest, directly over my heart,” Baldwin, 60, told People in an interview published on Wednesday, November 18. “It was almost like if I took a feather and I tickled the back of your hand. I felt this weird kind of tickling sensation on my skin, directly under my pectoral muscle.”

The Usual Suspects actor said he experienced the sensation again multiple times throughout the night, approximately every four hours.

“I woke up the next day, and immediately it was there again,” he recalled. “Nothing intense, no pain. Just a strange fluttering.”

Baldwin said he became alarmed when the fluttering increased to every two hours.

“I’m not a doctor, but I’ve played one on TV. And common sense would say, you know, my body’s saying something and I don’t know what it is,” he continued. “So, ​​I’m getting a little nervous.”

Thankfully, Baldwin already had an aortic specialist after his daughter Hailey Bieber encouraged him to keep an eye on his heart health four years ago. (Baldwin’s father had an aortic aneurysm, a balloon-like bulge in the aorta, before he died from lung cancer at age 55. Aortic issues can be hereditary.)

Baldwin recalled texting his specialist, who called him right away.

“He wastes no time. He just literally says to me these life-changing words: ‘Listen to me, and do exactly as I tell you. When you hang up this phone…’ And that’s when I knew something was wrong,” he continued.

Baldwin was referred to a cardiologist, who told him that he needed to go to the hospital. After blood tests, an ultrasound and a CT scan at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City, he was diagnosed with coronary artery disease (CAD).

According to the Mayo Clinic, CAD is a common type of heart disease that “affects the main blood vessels that supply blood to the heart, called the coronary arteries,” and reduces blood flow. A complete blockage of blood flow can lead to a heart attack, making the condition very serious.

Baldwin underwent a diagnostic procedure called a cardiac catheterization, which led doctors to discover that his left anterior descending (LAD) artery had a 90 percent blockage. They performed an angioplasty to open the blocked blood vessels and placed a stent.

Baldwin admitted that he got “pretty choked up” when he learned about the severity of his CAD.

“You just start to go through all of those thoughts in your head, like, what could have happened? That was kind of life-changing because I thought I was fine,” he told the outlet. “And that block didn’t just happen overnight. The calcification of the block was something that took years to develop.”

Baldwin recalled his doctor telling him, “‘You’re a very lucky guy. God has plans for you.’ For a surgeon, a guy who goes in and does this every day several times a day, to say that … it’s life-changing.”

Baldwin said the health scare led him to feel “born again” with a “new lease on life.”

“When you face your mortality in this way? That’s a wake-up call that now has become a bit of a mission for me,” he shared. “Hopefully I can be a part of communicating the importance of plaque tests, cholesterol checks, all of that.”

Baldwin concluded, “You have to do the research on your own body to make sure you’re OK. There’s enough information and enough science about how to be heart healthy. Once you turn 50, 55, 60, you have to do something to protect yourself so that your quality of life in your 70s, 80s, 90s is what it could potentially be. You’ve got to do what you have to do to live and stay alive and be healthy.”

Which historical figure do you most identify with?

My wife, Janice. Fearless, smart, optimistic, hilarious, loving…adored by all.

What is the trait you most deplore in yourself?

Self-doubt. Wait, now I’m not sure of the answer. Was that okay? Can we come back to that one?

What is the trait you most deplore in others?

From my dressing room to backstage—standing alone in the dark, a deep breath, and then feeling it’s time and walking out into the light.

What do you consider the most overrated virtue?

What do you dislike most about your appearance?

I’d rather not say, and thank you for your attention to this matter!

Which words or phrases do you most overuse?

“Sorry, I didn’t see your text till now.”

That my father died when I was 15 and never got to see my family, my career, and the man I think I am.

What or who is the greatest love of your life?

In the hospital waiting room, when my girls were born, and the doctor said everyone was fine.

Which talent would you most like to have?

If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be?

I’d stop worrying about everyone all the time.

That they’d finally understand why I worry about everyone all the time

We raised two fantastic daughters who became good, hard-working, honest people and great spouses and mothers in the middle of this business.

If you could choose what to come back as, what would it be?

I lost them all, so I’d have to say my memory.

What do you regard as the lowest depth of misery?

Love, empathy, loyalty, a sense of humor, and a handful of quarters for the parking meters.

TheÂ GTAÂ games are often story-generating machines. Part of the fun of playing them is getting to talk to your friends later about the wild encounters and experiences you had in-game. An anecdote about one such encounter from Jason Schreier’s review forÂ BloombergÂ seems to be persuading at least a few folks who previously weren’t interested in playing the game into potentially giving it a try.

It definitely makes for an attention-grabbing opener to the review. The anecdote reads:

Several hours into Grand Theft Auto VI, I watched a sedan get smashed from behind by a truck. I had been driving around Vice City, a fictionalized re-creation of Miami with such lifelike graphical fidelity that it can be hard to distinguish the video game from real-life footage, and I pulled to a stop when I saw the two vehicles collide. The truck driver scampered off, leaving the victim trapped in his seat as his engine began to catch fire. I ran over and helped him out of the car. He thanked me, reflecting in astonishment that heâd almost died. Then he noticed that the culprit was a delivery truck for Sahara, the Grand Theft Auto parody of Amazon. This was his big break, he declared. He could sue Sahara for millions.

But he needed demonstrable damages. So he took a deep breath, got back in the car, set his own legs on fire and then re-emerged with burns all over his body. He called his lawyer. Then, as an ambulance approached, he turned and asked me to be a witness in exchange for some of his inevitable payout. I thought about pressing a button to blackmail him but ultimately agreed to help, and he sent me a few thousand dollars on BuckMe, the gameâs version of Venmo.

This is the kind of encounter that Rockstar excels at, an event you just stumble upon that seems random but is actually crafted specifically to give the world that feeling of life, randomness, and spontaneity. And I’m sure this is just one of many such events you might come across in your time with the game.

It was enough to intrigue journalist and OnionÂ CEO Ben Collins, who posted the anecdote to Bluesky and said, “Had basically zero interest in playing GTA VI until I saw this lede in a Bloomberg review. It’s persuasive writing, at the very least.” Meanwhile,Â New York TimesÂ opinion columnist Jamelle Bouie also shared the opening to Schreier’s review on Bluesky and wrote, “This is honestly enough to get me to buy a PS5 and pick up this game.”

#3573. GTA 6 Gym Workouts Have A Useful Trick That Saves You A Lot Of Time

You won't get muscles in real life without putting in some work, but fortunately, leveling up your pectorals in Grand Theft Auto 6 is much less strenuous. The only cardio you'll need to do is a series of finger movements on your controller, but admittedly, getting either of the game's protagonists into shape can be time-consuming. Fortunately, there's a trick that can help you cut workout times in half, which I wish I could apply to real life as well.

Essentially, all you need to do in GTA 6 is make sure you're going to the gym as a couple. If you only focus on Jason or Lucia for a workout, then they'll gradually gain muscle and tone up on their own. But if you go as a pair, it doesn't matter who you work out with; both characters will gain and progress on their path toward becoming absolute units.

That makes for a quick way to bulk up, though we still need to talk about Jason's gym etiquette.

This isn't the first time GTA has introduced gym gameplay mechanics to keep your protagonist in shape; back in GTA: San Andreas, players could frequent locations across the map and work on CJ's appearance. Not only could he increase his muscle mass and stamina by pumping iron, but CJ could also learn new fighting styles from trainers along the way. Working out in GTA 6 also has benefits, as lifting weights can improve overall health, while cardio activities like running and biking improve stamina.

You can even track Jason and Lucia's workouts via a smartphone app, and there's an optimal time for them to train to maximize their efforts. You can do that either at a proper gym in the game world or, if you're on a budget, use the set of weights outside Jason's house.

With GTA 6 out in the wild, players are quickly discovering just how much there is to do in Rockstar's massive open-world game. If you're one of them and looking for tips and tricks, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for walkthroughs to help you out.

I’m pretty good about keeping an eye on the Christmas movies schedule, but I was a few days late to Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. (Can you blame a girl when Hallmark is over here dropping holiday time loop bangers?) The new romantic holiday comedy was written and filmed in Sweden, but you’d seemingly never know it from the English version, which is dubbed over in English, and has the actors’ mouths matching the English words, as well. Let's talk about this strange magic.

Listen, no one official at Netflix has confirmed they used AI technology to get the mouths to match the English words coming out of the cast’s mouths, but it’s clear there’s some hijinks going on. Things felt off within a couple of minutes of watching the 2026 movie release, but at first I couldn’t place where the weird vibes were coming from. Once I realized what was going on, I couldn’t stop staring at people’s mouths.

It was uncanny. It made the viewing experience weird. I didn’t particularly like it. And it turned a perfectly OK holiday film into something far stranger.

I’m not the only person to feel this way, either.

The Christmas Switch was made available for anyone with a Netflix subscription on November 12th, so it's been around for a few days. It’s currently in the Top 10 in the US, along with fellow Christmas flicks The Gospel of Christmas and A Dog’s Perfect Christmas. So, it’s safe to say a lot of people have witnessed this mouth edit phenomenon.

Many of those people have taken to places like Reddit to express nearly the same feelings I’ve had.

Listen, we all know dubbing is annoying in general. I’ve watched every season of the now-canceled Maxton Hall on Amazon Prime Video, and I don’t like the mouths not matching the English language version, either. Still, at least that feels authentic. And there’s always the option to watch just with subtitles. (This is true for The Christmas Switch too; it’s just not the option that comes up on English-language Netflix first.)

Netflix has a global audience the streamer has to cater to, and I get why the service would want to experiment with options when it comes to programming in multiple languages. It makes total sense, particularly given Netflix's opinion that most people are multitasking while screening, and they want the content to be as easy as possible. Yet, in practicality, right now, I can tell you straight up the viewing experience is not good. So, next year I’d love it if the “Christmas switch” the streamer was making was choosing regular dubbing for its viewers. Please and thank you.

#3571. GTA 6 Twitch Drops Are Live, Here’s How To Get Your Free Rewards

While you might be tempted to take a spin through Grand Theft Auto 6 right now, you might want to hold your horses and watch some gameplay instead. How to access GTA 6 Twitch drops

Once you're all set up, tune in to any Twitch Drop-enabled livestream during a live Twitch Drops period--November 18-30--and watch for a minimum of 60 minutes on a day to earn a chain badge from the GTA DVD Chest.

How to get GTA 6 Twitch drops

If you watch on six days, you'll unlock all six badges: Purple, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Miami Chain.

Each new or gifted subscription to a participating GTA 6 streamer will also unlock a GTA-themed sub badge and an emote, so you'll need three subs to unlock all six. Prime subs don't count.

Once you've collected all 12 badges, you'll unlock the Golden Iguana chat badge.

What GTA 6 Twitch drops can I earn?

One important thing to note is that these will be Twitch-exclusive drops, not in-game items for GTA 6. But if you want to assemble the collection of rewards, here's what you can get:

Daily Chests — GTA DVD Chest (Six Chain Badges)

  • Purple Chain: Unlocked after watching 1 day of GTA 6 during launch week
  • Bronze Chain: Unlocked after watching 2 days of GTA 6 during launch week
  • Silver Chain: Unlocked after watching 3 days of GTA 6 during launch week
  • Gold Chain: Unlocked after watching 4 days of GTA 6 during launch week
  • Diamond Chain: Unlocked after watching 5 days of GTA 6 during launch week
  • Miami Chain: Unlocked after watching 6 days of GTA 6 during launch week

Subscription Drops (Three Badges & Three Emotes)

Sub badge earned by subscribing to a GTA VI channel.

  • Welcome 2 Miami
  • Scored Big
  • Bleed Miami

Exclusive launch subscription emote.

  • BustedPlz
  • DinoBusted
  • SabaBusted

Final Grand Prize

  • Golden Iguana: Earned by securing all 12 preceding launch rewards.

Heist Train Badges

A bonus set of badges will also be available from November 18-30. If you contribute to a completed Hype Train level on any GTA 6 streamer's channel, you can earn this custom collection designed by /LumpyTouch.

You can also get GTA 6: Ultimate Edition for free

Twitch will also be giving away free codes for the GTA 6: Ultimate Edition, starting November 19 and running through November 30. Details for how you can receive a code have not been revealed yet, but we'll update this post once we have them.

GTA 6 Streamers to watch

You can select Find Streams to see a list of streamers participating in the promotion. Eligible channels will have a "Drop enabled" message at the top of their chat. Alternatively, you can follow these steps:

  • Select Search at the top of the page
  • Enter GTA 6 in the search bar

#3570. Man Kidnapped Teen Girl, Dog Before Abandoning Her 200 Miles Away From Home

An Ohio man found himself behind bars after he allegedly picked up a teenage girl and her labradoodle before abandoning her in Virginia nearly 200 miles away from her South Carolina home while keeping the dog for himself.

Darlington County Sheriff Michael August confirmed to Us that Matthew Morris Hawkins was charged with one count each of kidnapping, grand larceny and contributing to the delinquency of a minor following the incident that took place in August.

Authorities said that deputies responded to the victim’s home in Florence, South Carolina, on August 6 after they received a report regarding a missing juvenile, according to a Monday, November 16, press release.

A preliminary investigation was launched into the matter, and authorities concluded that Hawkins, 41, had gone to the 17-year-old girl’s home to pick up the teen and her dog.

Hawkins then allegedly took the teen to Martinsville, Virginia, where he subsequently “abandoned her.”

The defendant allegedly picked the girl up from her home at night without her parents’ knowledge or permission, according to an arrest warrant obtained by WBTW. One day after she went missing, Henry County Sheriff’s Office deputies found the girl in Virginia on August 7.

Troopers with the Kentucky State Police located Hawkins the following day on August 8 in Winchester, Virginia, and he was arrested without incident. Authorities reported that Hawkins allegedly had the girl’s labradoodle still in his possession at the time he was arrested.

Hawkins was taken into custody at the Clark County Detention Center in Kentucky before he was extradited to Henry County, Virginia. He was eventually extradited last week and processed at the W. Glenn Campbell Detention Center on Friday, November 13.

The defendant went on to make his first appearance in Darlington County District Court, where a magistrate judge ordered him to be held without bond.

It’s not currently clear whether Hawkins has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Darlington County Sheriff’s Office had no additional updates to share when contacted by Us about the case.

The investigation into Hawkins and the alleged kidnapping remains active as police work to determine what events led up to his arrest.

Authorities have not yet revealed how Hawkins and the victim first connected or how long they were communicating prior to the alleged kidnapping.

#3568. GTA 6 Has A Clever PS5 DualSense Trick For Keeping You Under The Speed Limit

While the urge to be an absolute menace in Grand Theft Auto 6 is strong, nothing stops you from playing as a law-abiding citizen who sticks to the speed limit between missions. This option to avoid attracting local law enforcement's attention will probably be best experienced on PS5, thanks to one key advantage: the DualSense controller and its adaptive triggers.

On PS5, GTA 6 players can keep their vehicle from going over the speed limit, as the adaptive triggers provide resistance when you get close to the legal limit. That doesn't mean that you can't break past that barrier, but the adaptive triggers will help you match traffic speed most of the time and stick to legal restrictions. That essentially makes it easier to control your vehicle and gives your index fingers a sense of how hard to press the triggers--useful when you're trying to avoid dinging your car by finding that sweet spot.

This is just one of several vehicle-specific features in GTA 6, as the game borrows a few ideas from modern-day open-world games and puts its own spin on it. For example, you can summon your car via a smartphone app, which involves a Scooter Bros. employee appearing at your location, delivering your ride, and then disappearing into the sunset with the little two-wheeled ride they stashed in your trunk.

Cars appear to be more important than ever in GTA 6, and stealing a fresh set of wheels is also something that has a little more friction to it, as you could boost a junker with an empty tank of fuel or an expensive sports car that has GPS tracking inside of it.

If you're making the trip to Vice City this month, you can check out GameSpot's comprehensive Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub for plenty of tips and tricks.

#3567. Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a new era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Although a new era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had announced that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he said to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

Almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was announced that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

Although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit big with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

The Brady Bunch alum Barry Williams gave his all throughout Dancing With the Stars, which admittedly took him a while to recuperate from after leaving the ballroom competition.

“At Dancing with the Stars, I brought out 100 percent of everything; everything I had. I have never been so tested,” Williams, 72, said on a recent episode of the “Pop Culture Preservation Society” podcast. “I’m not going to lie: There was a year of recovery after those two, three months.”

Williams danced with DWTS pro Peta Murgatroyd on 2023’s season 32, finishing in seventh place.

“There’s no way that you can actually practice for ballroom. It is completely different,” the actor acknowledged. “It is like what pop music dancing is to ballet is what ballroom is to pop, and so it helps to have a really, really great partner, and I did, [and] that is what really carried it. Whatever it was going to be, I just knew that I would leave it all on the dance floor. [I had a] great time.”

Throughout his ballroom tenure, Williams even had his family, friends, Brady costars and fans rooting for success.

“There is a lot of support and with this show, not only friends and your family involved, but fans, and then they participate in the process so that people are voting,” he told Us exclusively in October 2023. “They’re actively a part of it. They get to share the joy of moving forward to the next week when I can take up their time for another Tuesday night.”

In particular, Williams felt “great” as he learned to nail the dance steps and improve his overall stamina.

“I think it feels like it’s starting over each week because we start a new dance,” he acknowledged at the time. “It has a new impulse … and it’s unfamiliar to me, so it’s not part of my wheelhouse. The most difficult part is to readapt every week.”

Weeks after Williams’ elimination, actress Xochitl Gomez and pro dancer Val Chmerkovskiy clinched the mirrorball trophy.

#3565. GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before

Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, off its throne? The answer is a resounding yes: not only is GTA 6 being reviewed higher than Nintendo's little hero in green, but it's also emerging as one of the highest-rated games of all time.

When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 147 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score.

GTA 6 is only the second game to earn a metascore of 98, and hilariously, it's tied with the original Ocarina of Time from 1998. Historically, GTA games have always had some of the highest review aggregates, especially after the series moved to the third dimension. Starting with GTA 3, mainline entries have all earned metascores in the high 90s, with Grand Theft Auto 4 being the highest-reviewed game in the franchise until GTA 6 came along. Here's a closer look at those metascores over the years.:

  • Grand Theft Auto — No metascore
  • Grand Theft Auto 2 — 70
  • Grand Theft Auto 3 — 97
  • Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — 95
  • Grand Theft Auto 4 — 98
  • Grand Theft Auto 5 — 97

Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it.

"This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's GTA 6 review.

If you're planning to start playing it, you can also check out GameSpot's massive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips and tricks you need to explore Vice City.

#3564. Rockstar Explains Why GTA 6 Has No Prostitutes In It, A Hallmark Of The Series Since 2001

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a very big game and includes almost every feature seen in a past GTA game, including the ability to drive tanks, customize cars with turbo, and rob stores. However, one feature that isn’t included in GTA 6 is the ability to hire a sex worker off the street, something players have been doing since 2001.

In my over 150 hours playing GTA 6, which is a very good game in case you didn’t hear already, I never encountered a sex worker on the streets of Vice City. To be honest, I never really sought out prostitutes, as I was roleplaying Jason and Lucia as a loving couple who cared about each other deeply. But yeah, when I did look around for sex workers walking the street, I didn’t spot any. And that’s because Rockstar Games didn’t include them in GTA 6.

In an interview with Shack News, Rockstar said that it only included features that felt necessary and complementary to Jason and Lucia’s criminal tale.

âGTA VI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run,” said Rockstar. “While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand uponâthings like the wanted system, the radio, robberies, and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA VI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story.â

The first Grand Theft Auto game to include prostitutes that players could hire was GTA 3, released in 2001. Since then, every mainline GTA game has included sex workers that players can pay for services. However, GTA 6 is breaking that 25-year trend, and honestly, I didn’t even notice until someone else pointed it out online. Turns out, the ability to hire prostitutes isn’t necessary to make a good GTA.

There are still strip clubs with plenty of nudity in GTA 6. And you can always come home and make Jason and Lucia have sex if you want some fun.

#3561. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

#3558. GTA 6 Passes 17 Million Copies Sold And $1.6 Billion In Revenue On Eve Of Launch

The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 17.07 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.65 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 12.73 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 4.35 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 17.07 million GTA 6 sales so far, 75% are on PS5 and 25% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.23 billion in revenue, compared to $419 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

Survivor looks way easier than it really is.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There are few reality TV shows with the legacy of Survivor, which is currently airing its whopping 51st season on CBS (and streaming with a Paramount+ subscription). Apart from how much money Survivor players make, fans are also curious about how the various challenges come together. It turns out that Christian Chavez's boat ride from last week was actually a bit of a nightmare for production to figure out.

Survivor's Open Era is here, and every episode of Season 51 has brought at least one new twist. Prior to the baffling tribal council and double elimination, Christian took a boat to a sandspit in the middle of the ocean, and fought to keep his vote and gain an extra one. Over on Survivor's Instagram, host/producer Jeff Probst wrote about the logistics that went into this scene, starting with:

This spot is one of the most beautiful spots in all of Fiji and for a very short period of time each day you can actually go there and stand on the spit before the water rises so much that the entire spit disappears. It's visually spectacular but scheduling is everything as the window is tiny.

Talk about a logistical puzzle. Survivor is a huge production, but I never thought about how things like the tide and crew members made things even more complicated. It turns out that there was a very limited window where Christian could take the boat to the sandspit, and do the buoy challenge that would determine how many votes (if any) he'd have during the "double duo" week.

Most challenges have a time limit for the players, but for Christian's journey there was also a limited amount of time where the sandspit would still be walkable before being swallowed up by the sea. As host Jeff Probst continued to explain in his field notes:

So the minute a decision was made on who would take the journey we went into action- the transport boat is ready, drones are in the air, camera and audio crews waiting at the sandspit and Team Flint is always there to oversee and ensure the challenge plays as it should. When it all works you get a really great moment that can only happen on a show like ours.

Well, my mind is spinning. As a longtime fan of the show, the difficulty of shooting the show is sometimes lost on me. After all, I'm usually more invested in the gameplay, and how well my Survivor draft picks are doing. There's so much that goes into each season's production that we never think of, which is why I appreciate Probst giving us these details about how it all comes together.

New episodes of Survivor air Wednesdays on CBS as part of the 2026 TV schedule. I can't wait to see the fallout from last week, including Eric's wild decision not to use Christian's extra vote... especially after hearing how hard the journey was to shoot.

#3556. Want A Custom GTA 6 PS5 Pro? Just Play In The NBA

PS5 Pro consoles have been hard to find lately, but there is a trick to getting one: All you need is superb basketball skills and membership on an NBA team based in the state that inspired Grand Theft Auto 6's location. Easy! While it's a little too late to take advantage of this life hack now, things have worked out for the Miami Heat, as they were gifted a unique set of PS5 Pro consoles this week.

Miami Heat player Myron Gardner posted a photo of the care package that arrived for him, which includes the aforementioned PS5 Pro console, two officially licensed GTA 6 DualSense controllers, and a physical copy of the game, all sealed in a padded case. Compared to the recent, flashy PS5 console covers, this variant of the beefy PS5 has a more subtle design, combining a matte black finish with the GTA 6 logo, palm tree silhouettes, and neon-inspired colors on the console's physical stripes.

The consoles will likely be a small incentive for the Miami Heat team, as they'll be representing their city and GTA 6 when they hit the court tonight for a match against the Milwaukee Bucks. Developer Rockstar Games and publisher Take-Two Interactive have taken over the Miami Heat stadium, decking it out in custom GTA 6 graphics and insignia for the basketball game, as well as custom uniforms for the team. The Miami Heat are the odds-on favorites to win, as they've enjoyed a five-game winning streak lately, while the Milwaukee Bucks are looking to break their current losing streak, which is now 10 games long.

The A Night in Vice City basketball game is set to be a big attraction, as it'll cap off the global rollout of GTA 6 tonight when the game unlocks in the US. Already active in several other time zones at the time of writing, GTA 6 has received overwhelmingly positive reviews and is the highest-rated game of the year. "Rockstar’s most ambitious game yet was worth the wait," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's GTA 6 review.

With an absolutely massive sandbox and tons to do, it's a good idea to consult a few walkthroughs to help you keep track of everything. GameSpot’s GTA 6 guides hub lets you do just that, and it will be continually updated with new tips and tricks in the weeks and months to come.
